Title: King Tides and Climate Change
Content: `text(Spring)` tides are extremely high tides that occur when `text(Earth)`, the `text(Moon)`, and the `text(Sun)` are aligned. A king tide is the common name given to an extremely high `text(spring)` tide that occurs at perigee (when the `text(Moon)` is closest to `text(Earth)` in its orbit). King tides occur `text(once)` or `text(twice every year)`.

Normal high tides are now reaching higher and extending farther inland than in the past because of global climate change and rising sea levels. This causes low-lying shorelines to be at an increased risk of flooding. If climate continues to change and sea levels rise, `text(spring)` tides and king tides will have a greater effect on shorelines and coastal flooding.
